# Error codes

Every BHMS error code: the JSON-RPC number, the default retry class, what it means, and where it can appear. The table is the code table of [spec 10.2](../../../spec/bhms/10-errors.md#102-code-table); the generator checks that the Python SDK (`bhms.protocol.errors.CODES`), the schema (`x-bhms-errors`) and the TypeScript SDK (`CODES` in `sdk/typescript/src/errors.ts`) carry exactly the same numbers and retry classes.

An error response is `{code, message, data: {bhmsCode, field?, bound?, operationId?, mayHaveActed, retry, hint}}`. In Python it is raised as `bhms.BhmsError` with the attributes `bhms_code`, `field`, `bound`, `operation_id`, `may_have_acted`, `retry` and `hint`; in TypeScript as `BhmsError` with `bhmsCode`, `field`, `bound`, `operationId`, `mayHaveActed`, `retry` and `hint`. An admitted operation that ends `failed`, `rejected` or `unknown` carries the same members in `operation.error`.

Retry classes: `never` (change the request first), `backoff` (try again later, with the same operation key), `after-reconcile` (read the operation's state, then decide), `same-key` (retry with the same key).

| Code | JSON-RPC | Retry | Appears as | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | -32602 | `never` | error response or operation error | Malformed params, unknown member, wrong type, unknown property/operation/cursor/digest |
| `OUT_OF_RANGE` | -32602 | `never` | error response or operation error | A value outside the effective envelope or a limit |
| `UNIT_MISMATCH` | -32602 | `never` | error response or operation error | A quantity in a unit other than the declared one; nothing is converted silently |
| `UNKNOWN_DEVICE` | -32001 | `never` | error response or operation error | Device id not registered or not visible |
| `UNKNOWN_ACTION` | -32002 | `never` | error response or operation error | Action not on the device |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | -32003 | `never` | error response or operation error | Capability, method or requirement not available; refuse rather than emulate |
| `LEASE_REQUIRED` | -32004 | `never` | error response or operation error | The action needs a lease; acquire one first |
| `LEASE_CONFLICT` | -32005 | `backoff` | error response or operation error | Another principal holds a needed resource, or the lease is not the caller's |
| `LEASE_EXPIRED` | -32006 | `never` | error response or operation error | The lease expired or is unknown; reacquire |
| `FENCED` | -32007 | `never` | error response or operation error | The lease was superseded or revoked; reacquire |
| `KEY_CONFLICT` | -32008 | `never` | error response or operation error | `operationKey` reused for a different intent |
| `STALE` | -32009 | `after-reconcile` | error response or operation error | A precondition is unmet: stale observation, changed description, unresolved unknown operation, failed assert |
| `DEVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | -32010 | `backoff` | error response or operation error | Device offline or unreachable |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | -32011 | `never` | error response or operation error | The principal lacks the scope |
| `BUSY` | -32012 | `backoff` | error response or operation error | Device or server saturated |
| `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | -32013 | `after-reconcile` | error response or operation error | A deadline or duration bound passed, or a reply was lost; the code of every operation that becomes `unknown` (BHMS-OPS-004) |
| `INTERNAL` | -32014 | `never` | error response or operation error | Server bug |
| `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | -32015 | `never` | error response or operation error | Protocol version not served; `bound` lists supported versions |
| `UNVERIFIED` | -32016 | `after-reconcile` | operation error only | Required measured evidence was absent or contradicted the effect |
| `DEVICE_FAULT` | -32017 | `after-reconcile` | operation error only | The device reported a fault while acting; partial effects possible |

`mayHaveActed` is the member to branch on: `false` means nothing reached the device, `true` means it may have acted (the operation becomes `unknown` rather than `failed` when nobody can say). `OUT_OF_RANGE` with a `field` that starts with `result.` is a measurement outside the action's declared output range (the device acted), not a refused request.
